turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on days and months?
turns.tutor:
Days and months come soon. We start with clock times. Here is one example, step by step. Sentence: The film starts ___ eight. Step 1: I look at the time word: "eight". Step 2: it is a time on the clock. Step 3: so I use "at". Result: The film starts at eight.
The rule: use at before a time on the clock.
Right: We have dinner at half past six. Wrong: We have dinner on half past six.
Your turn. Write in, on or at: My train leaves ___ 5 o'clock.
